findings.reason: a node that changes only the cited expression leaves its own first done-when case failing on a same-content store, and if it then repairs `review_coverage` to pass, it changes a gate's verdict the plan never mentions.
findings.text: §43 says "`read_plan_review` picks among the covering reviews with `max(covering, key=plan_version)` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py` near line 1269), so a tie resolves to the first record read, the oldest", but a tie is also resolved one layer down: `review_coverage` takes `newest = max(whole, key=plan_version)` at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1024` and returns `[newest]` — a single-element list — at :1028 and :1039 whenever the stored reviews' `plan_fingerprint` matches the plan's current content, which is exactly the construction the done-when's "temporary store holding two reviews of one plan at the same `plan_version`" produces. In that path `read_plan_review`'s `covering` at :1262-1269 holds one record, so the change the deliverable names cannot make done-when case 1 return the newer review; the tie-break has to be corrected in `review_coverage` too. That same function is the plan-review gate's reader (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2720`), so the corrected tie also changes which review a dispatch hold reads.

rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate log is named to the run directory and ends in a bare `EXIT=` line; no scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, filename or comment in the declared write paths.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the deliverable locates the tie at `read_plan_review`'s single `max`, but `review_coverage` resolves the same tie first and hands `read_plan_review` a one-element list.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one verdict (an answer reaches the newest review that raised the finding), whose parts are the tie-break, the CLI route and the MCP route.
